trStyle: Style: write like a friendly senior Pakistani developer explaining to a colleague, in the natural Urdu-English mix Pakistani developers really speak. Address the reader as "aap". Keep these in English exactly as they are (never translate): technology and product names (Laravel, PHP, React, MySQL, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Shopify...), SQL keywords (SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY...), and everyday dev words such as API, request, response, server, client, database, table, row, column, query, index, cache, queue, job, event, middleware, route, controller, model, migration, deploy, bug, debug, performance, scale, load balancer, microservice, token, session, cookie, frontend, backend, framework, function, class, object, array, loop, error, exception, test, commit, branch, container, filter, sort, default. The CORE CONCEPT must be in clear, natural PAKISTANI Urdu — use Urdu/Perso-Arabic words, not Sanskritised Hindi: masla (not samasya), waqt (not samay), zaroori (not aavashyak), istemal (not prayog), maqsad (not uddeshya), tafseel (not vistaar), sawal/jawab (not prashn/uttar), misaal (not udaharan), farq (not antar), tareeqa (not vidhi), koshish (not prayas), faida/nuqsaan (not laabh/haani), mehfooz (not surakshit), mumkin (not sambhav), shuru/khatam (not aarambh/samaapt), tezi (not gati), hisaab, aasan, mushkil. Explain hard ideas with one short everyday Pakistani example (a dukaan, a bank line, a school register, a courier, cricket) when it helps. Keep numbers, identifiers and commands exactly as in the source. Keep every key point; do not add facts that are not in the source.
hiStyle: Style: write like a friendly senior Indian developer explaining to a colleague, in simple everyday spoken Hindi — the natural Hindi-English mix (Hinglish) developers really speak. Avoid heavy Sanskrit words: say "zaroori" not "aavashyak", "use karna" not "prayog karna", "fayda" not "laabh", "problem/dikkat" not "samasya", "matlab" not "arth", "example" or "misaal" not "udaharan". Keep technology names, SQL keywords and everyday dev words (API, query, table, column, index, cache, server, database, function, class, error, deploy...) in English, in Latin letters. Explain hard ideas with one short everyday example. Keep numbers, identifiers and commands exactly as in the source. Keep every key point; do not add facts that are not in the source.
ruSpell: Roman Urdu spelling — Pakistani WhatsApp style, one consistent spelling: hai, hain, ho, tha, thi, ka, ki, ke, ko, se, mein, par, aur, ya, nahi, kya, kyun, kaise, kab, jab, tab, agar, lekin, bhi, sirf, yeh, woh, is, us, iska, uska, apna, hota hai, hoti hai, karta hai, karte hain, kar sakte hain, zaroori, masla, faida, nuqsaan, tareeqa, matlab, misaal, yaani, pehle, baad mein, jaldi, aasan, mushkil, sawal, jawab, zyada, kam, waqt, cheez, sab, har, farq, istemal, maqsad. Write long vowels as aa/ee/oo, q for ق, kh for خ, gh for غ, z for ز/ذ/ض/ظ, f for ف.
